solution: The volume is \(|D|\), where \(D=\begin{vmatrix}1&a&1\\0&1&a\\a&0&1\end{vmatrix}=1(1-0)-a(0-a^{2})+1(0-a)=a^{3}-a+1\). Let \(f(a)=a^{3}-a+1\); \(f'(a)=3a^{2}-1=0\) gives \(a=\pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), and \(f''(a)=6a>0\) at \(a=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), a local minimum, where \(f=1-\frac{2}{3\sqrt{3}}>0\) is the volume itself. Matches option C.
note: volume written |a^3 - a|; the determinant is a^3 - a + 1. Key C unchanged.

solution: \(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\), of magnitude 3. From \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}=|\vec{c}|\) and \(|\vec{c}-\vec{a}|^{2}=8\): \(|\vec{c}|^{2}-2|\vec{c}|+9=8\), so \(|\vec{c}|=1\). Then \(|(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\times\vec{c}|=|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}||\vec{c}|\sin30^{\circ}=3\cdot1\cdot\frac{1}{2}=\frac{3}{2}\). Matches option A.
note: a x b written -2i + 2j + k; it is 2i - 2j + k (same magnitude); |c| = 1 now derived. Key A unchanged.

solution: The angle is obtuse when \(\bar p\cdot\bar q<0\) for every \(y\): \(my^{2}+6my-12<0\). For \(m<0\) this holds for all \(y\) exactly when the discriminant is negative: \(36m^{2}+48m<0\Rightarrow12m(3m+4)<0\Rightarrow-\dfrac{4}{3}<m<0\). Matches option D.
note: the discriminant condition was written > 0 (inverted); it must be < 0 for the quadratic to stay negative. Key D unchanged.

solution: \(|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|^{2}=16-4=12\). \(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}=2\vec{b}\cdot(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})-3|\vec{b}|^{2}=0-48=-48\). Since \(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\perp\vec{b}\), \(|\vec{c}|^{2}=4\cdot12+9\cdot16=192\), so \(|\vec{c}|=8\sqrt{3}\). \(\cos\theta=\dfrac{-48}{8\sqrt{3}\cdot4}=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\), so \(\theta=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\). Matches option B.
note: the denominator was written 2 sqrt12 x 4; |c| = 8 sqrt3. Key B unchanged.

solution: \((\vec{u}-\vec{v})\times(\vec{v}-\vec{w})=\vec{u}\times\vec{v}-\vec{u}\times\vec{w}+\vec{v}\times\vec{w}\). Dotting with \(\vec{u}+\vec{v}-\vec{w}\), every term with a repeated vector vanishes, leaving \(\vec{u}\cdot(\vec{v}\times\vec{w})-\vec{v}\cdot(\vec{u}\times\vec{w})-\vec{w}\cdot(\vec{u}\times\vec{v})=[\vec{u}\,\vec{v}\,\vec{w}]+[\vec{u}\,\vec{v}\,\vec{w}]-[\vec{u}\,\vec{v}\,\vec{w}]=\vec{u}\cdot(\vec{v}\times\vec{w})\). Matches option A.
note: claimed only one triple product survives; three survive and two cancel. Key A unchanged.

solution: Expanding the scalar triple product: \(f(x)=x^{3}-27x+26\). \(f'(x)=0\Rightarrow x=\pm3\); \(f''(3)>0\) so \(x_{0}=3\). \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=-2x-2x-3=-4(3)-3=-15\). Matches option B: \(-15\).
note: constant term written 28; it is 26 (no effect on x0). Key B unchanged.

solution: From \(\vec{b}\times(\vec{c}-\vec{a})=\vec{0}\), \(\vec{c}-\vec{a}=\lambda\vec{b}\). Using \(\vec{c}\cdot\vec{a}=0\): \(|\vec{a}|^{2}+\lambda(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})=0\), i.e. \(6+4\lambda=0\), so \(\lambda=-\frac{3}{2}\). Then \(\vec{c}\cdot\vec{b}=\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}+\lambda|\vec{b}|^{2}=4-\frac{3}{2}\cdot3=-\frac{1}{2}\). Matches option D: \(-\frac{1}{2}\).
note: lambda was given as -(a.b)/|b|^2; it is -|a|^2/(a.b) = -3/2. Key D unchanged.

solution: By BAC-CAB, \(\hat{i}\times(\vec{a}\times\hat{i})=\vec{a}-(\vec{a}\cdot\hat{i})\hat{i}\), and likewise for \(\hat{j}\) and \(\hat{k}\). Adding, \(\vec{b}=3\vec{a}-\vec{a}=2\vec{a}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\), so \(|\vec{b}|=\sqrt{4+16+36}=\sqrt{56}=2\sqrt{14}\). Matches option D.
note: the sum was written 2a - (i + j + k); it is 3a - a = 2a. Key D unchanged.

solution: The bisector of \(\vec{b}\) and \(\vec{c}\) lies along \(\hat{b}+\hat{c}=\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{\hat{j}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{2}}\), so \(\vec{a}=\lambda(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k})\). Matching the \(\hat{j}\) component, \(2\lambda=2\Rightarrow\lambda=1\), so \(\alpha=1,\beta=1\). Matches option A.
note: the bisector was written lambda(i + j + k) times a garbled root; it is along i + 2j + k. Key A unchanged.
